description: Calque Batch 2: 'say with <person pronoun>' -> 'say to <person pronoun>' (rule en-calque-say-with-person). VN learners calque 'noi voi' as 'say with' where English uses the indirect-object 'say to'. V1 fires only on say/says/said/saying + with + an allowlisted person-pronoun tail when 'with <pronoun>' is the immediate complement; it blocks intervening direct objects, fronted wh-object questions, parentheticals, absolute/comitative 'with', and non-'say' verbs. expectedStatus/expectedCorrection are the VERIFIED output of correctWithTutorRules('en') on current main (every case probed against the live engine; intended spec outputs all matched actual).
fp_risk_note: High FP risk: 'with' is valid in comitative/absolute constructions (with him present / gone / there; beside me), after an intervening object (say it with; say the truth with), in parentheticals set off by commas (I would say, with him, that ...), with a different verb (talked/went with her), and in wh-object questions (what / which sentence are you saying with them?). None of these are indirect-object 'say to <pronoun>', so the rule must NOT fire. The hardest guards are the intervening-object case ('She said the truth with him') and the wh-object question ('Which sentence are you saying with them?') — a naive say...with-<pronoun> matcher over-fires there; the live engine correctly leaves both unchanged.

positive.input: I want to say with you.
positive.expectedCorrection: I want to say to you.
positive.notes: Base infinitive 'say with you' -> 'say to you'.
Past 'said with me' -> 'said to me'; trailing time adverbial untouched.

positive.input: He says with her every day.
positive.expectedCorrection: He says to her every day.

positive.input: They are saying with us now.
positive.expectedCorrection: They are saying to us now.
positive.notes: Progressive 'are saying with us' -> 'are saying to us'.

positive.input: Please say with them after class.
positive.expectedCorrection: Please say to them after class.

negative.notes: FP guard (intervening direct object 'it'): 'with me' is comitative, not the indirect object. WATCH case — must not fire.

negative.input: She said with him beside me.
negative.expectedCorrection: She said with him beside me.
negative.notes: FP guard (absolute/comitative 'with him beside me'): not an indirect object.

negative.input: I would say, with him, that it's wrong.
negative.expectedCorrection: I would say, with him, that it's wrong.
negative.notes: FP guard (parenthetical 'with him' set off by commas): not the complement of 'say'.

negative.input: What are you saying with them?
negative.expectedCorrection: What are you saying with them?
negative.notes: FP guard (wh-object question): fronted 'what' is the object; 'with them' is comitative. WATCH case.
FP guard (different verb 'talked'): 'talk with' is correct English, not a calque.

negative.input: She said the truth with him.
negative.expectedCorrection: She said the truth with him.
negative.notes: FP guard (intervening object 'the truth'): the WATCH over-fire case — engine correctly does not insert 'to'.

negative.input: Which sentence are you saying with them?
negative.expectedCorrection: Which sentence are you saying with them?
negative.notes: FP guard (wh-object question with object 'which sentence'): the WATCH over-fire case — engine correctly leaves it unchanged.
FP guard (different verb 'went'): 'go with' is correct comitative English. (Retained from the original a1 fixture.)
FP guard (intervening object 'it' + manner 'with confidence'): not an indirect object. (Retained from the original a1 fixture.)
